text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.3% today to $153.45, extending a four-day rally that's pushed the stock up nearly 5% over two weeks. The immediate catalyst is a surge in refining profits across Big Oil, driven by geopolitical disruptions: Ukrainian and Russian strikes have damaged refineries in both countries, spiking global diesel prices and widening the gap between crude costs and refined product sales. Competitors Chevron, Exxon, and BP all hit record highs or posted massive profit beats on the same dynamics, pulling ConocoPhillips higher in the sector's momentum.

The underlying tailwind is the spread between world crude (now $123/barrel) and US crude ($103/barrel)—a $20 gap that reflects supply stress from Middle East and Russia-Ukraine tensions. Refining margins have become unusually profitable precisely because these geopolitical frictions are constraining refinery capacity while keeping shipping lanes tense, which benefits integrated energy companies sitting on both crude extraction and refining operations.
